text: Segment-pen protocol: abstract pens, BasePen and segment decomposition. A pen standardises how outlines are drawn: outline.draw(pen) makes the outline call moveTo , lineTo , curveTo , qCurveTo , closePath / endPath and addComponent on the pen. This module is a dependency-free port of the fontTools module so FontLab code can speak the protocol without fontTools. BasePen subclasses override _moveTo , _lineTo , _curveToOne (and optionally _qCurveToOne , _closePath , _endPath ); it splits super-beziers and TrueType quadratic strings, including the off-curve-only None form.

text: Pens and readers over FontGate ( fontgate.fg* ) layers and elements. Targets are an fgLayer or an fgShape (element), never an fgGlyph . Writing to a layer creates one new element for the pen session; writing to an element appends to it. Each contour is validated in Python first, then stored with a single contour.nodes = [...] assignment (point names and smooth flags kept). FontGate components are glyph-level only, so addComponent raises ComponentError . Empty native contours are never handed to native drawPoints , which dereferences the first node unchecked. The native fgPen fast path is not offered: it binds to a glyph's work shape, which conflicts with the layer/element rule.

text: Pens and readers over FontLab ( fontlab.fl* ) layers and elements. Targets are an flLayer or an flShape (element), never an flGlyph . Contours are staged and validated in Python; close() (or leaving the with block) writes them: a layer gets one new flShape holding all of them, an element gets them appended. On a layer, addComponent is staged too and close() adds the component elements and the contour shape in call order. An exception in the drawing body writes nothing; a native commit failure may leave partial geometry. The pen is spent even when a commit or notify fails. An element cannot hold components, and a component element cannot take contours. No undo history is recorded unless notify="title" is given for an attached layer. Notification can change unrelated native timestamps; whole-font history preservation is not guaranteed. Bare elements do not support notification.
title: fontlab_pens.fontlab

text: Qt controls for FontLab objects and FontParts-style fonts. Qt loads only at construction. What it holds: the general browsers, previews, features editor and Designspace panel, the Qt lifetime base ( lifecycle ), the pure models, the sequence canvas, and the editors for FontParts-style fonts: font info, groups, kerning, transform, batch and glyph sequence. fontlabapp.fontui.feature_blocks reads and writes exact VFJ feature source through Fontport. Lazy by design: this module imports no editor module and no PythonQt. A factory imports its module only when you call it, which keeps the FontLab 5 s cold-import limit. Fontport: the FontParts editors validate and apply data with fontlab_fontport . That package depends on this one, so it is an optional extra: pip install "fontlab-fontlabapp[fontport]" . Without it, calling one of those factories raises ImportError that names the extra. Everything else here works without Fontport. Moved back (issue 201): fontlab_fontport.ui held these editors for one release. Fontport now has no UI; its ui package only raises ImportError . old: from fontlab_fontport.ui import kerning_editor new: from fly.ap.fontui import kerning_editor
title: fontlabapp.fontui

text: vfjo: VFJ Objects, a Box-based workflow over FontLab 9.1 object JSON. What: fontlabapp.vfjo casts the object JSON of fontlabapp.objects.json_data onto python-box, so glyphs, layers, elements, contours, anchors and hints read and edit as attributes. It adds safe whole-object edits ( move , scale , rename , set_width , add_suffix , edit_nodes ) and paste into the font with Undo. nodes holds the node-string model ( Node ). How: loads / load / from_glyphs / from_clipboard return Objects ; Objects.data is the box tree. Data is validated by json_data.Envelope.parse on the way in and out. Reading a missing key raises; a misspelt new key on a known level raises; add_key adds a key on purpose. move and scale change element transforms (components and transformed elements) or nodes, and anchors, guidelines and hints follow, so the data stays consistent. edit_nodes refuses to change a contour's point count (hints address points by index). Undo: only paste (and Objects.paste ) changes a font. Glyph data becomes new glyphs through json_data.paste_glyphs : Edit > Undo removes them one step per new glyph plus one for the outlines ( GLYPHS_UNDO_TEXT ). Layer, element and contour data is added to the current glyph's active layer through json_data.paste_shapes as one step; with font= it must be the current font. available , NEEDS_91 , PARTIAL_TEXT , GLYPHS_UNDO_TEXT and PartialWriteError are re-exported so scripts need only vfjo . Limits: never reads FontLab's vic/* clipboard (that binding crashes 9.1.9812, Fontlab/fl#8655). Checked live in FontLab 9.1.9812 with Lato and python-box 7.4.1: from_glyphs(["o", "Aogonek"]) , add_suffix , move(40, 0) , set_width(w + 80) and paste gave correct nodes, anchors, component offsets and widths in both masters; a misspelt read raised BoxKeyError and a misspelt write UnknownKeyError . scale , Undo and shape paste are not yet checked live. How to use:: from fontlabapp import vfjo objs = vfjo.from_glyphs(["o"]) # selected glyphs by default vfjo.add_suffix(objs, ".shift") vfjo.move(objs, 100, 0); vfjo.set_width(objs, lambda w: w + 200) objs.paste() # new glyph o.shift, with Undo

text: Shared plan and write kernel of the anchor writer scripts. What: the Anchors scripts (Rename Bulk, Center Horizontally, Place From Bounds, Snap To Metrics, Round To Grid, Delete By Name, Mirror Across Masters) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows. Each row can hold one Edit : ("set", name, (x, y)) : move the anchor; add it when it is missing; ("remove", name, None) : delete every anchor with this name; ("rename", name, new) : rename every anchor with this name. collect runs the planner on every editable layer and returns a Plan . require_safe refuses the whole batch before any history exists. apply_work writes all edits as ONE native Undo step and reads every value back. How: apply_work builds every native pin and point first ( prepare ), then calls fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit with operation="geometry" . The commit discloses queued native updates and refuses auto layers in the edit list, glyphs that own an auto layer and bases of auto composites (also through other composites). Then it inits history, runs write , stamps the glyphs, sends one notification and stamps again. unstored is the read-back: a value that FontLab did not keep raises RuntimeError . A failure after history started raises history.PartialWriteError ("... use Edit > Undo"). Why: FontLab cannot Redo an existing anchor moved to 0, 0 (FontLab issue 8527), so require_safe refuses that move. A new pin gets its name-derived appearance now ( anchor_copy.APPEARANCE ), because FontLab infers it only on Redo or reopen. An existing pin keeps its own style and expressions: write edits the existing pin object in place. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time. PythonQt, FontLab and anchor_copy load inside the functions, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. The panel base is in fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model . Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.anchors.panel.model as anchor_panel import fly.ap.anchors.writer as anchor_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): return [anchor_writer.Change("top", "1, 2", "0, 2", ("set", "top", (0, 2)))] class Panel(anchor_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY = "Example", "anchors_example" def planner(self): return planner

text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the anchor writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns AnchorPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Anchors scripts: script controls, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. ERROR_COLOR colours blocked rows; MAX_ROWS limits the preview rows. How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.anchors.writer ( collect , blocked_rows , require_safe ) on every control change, and Apply plans again from live data and writes with anchor_writer.apply_work (one Undo step). Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect in closeEvent . Why: the seven Anchors scripts then hold only their planner, a small panel subclass and main . This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.anchors.panel.ui . So FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast, and tests without Qt can import it. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.anchors.panel.model as anchor_panel class RoundToGrid(anchor_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION = "Round Anchors to Grid", "anchors_round_to_grid", "Round" def build_controls(self): ... def planner(self): ...

text: Non-modal panel: script controls, live preview table, Reload, Close, Apply. What: a subclass sets TITLE , KEY , ACTION (the Apply button text) and HEADERS (3 or 4 columns), and fills in build_controls and planner . Optional hooks: chosen_masters , glyph_names and on_reload . Helpers for subclasses: watch , spin , scope_box . How: every control change recomputes the plan from the live font and shows exactly what Apply would write. Apply stays off while any row is blocked or require_safe refuses. Apply binds to the font, master and glyphs of the last scan, plans again, scans the auto-layer facts again and writes once through anchor_writer.apply_work . Why: the preview can never be stale at Apply, and an exception in a slot stays in the status line instead of reaching FontLab. Show it with scripting.show_script_dialog(Subclass, Subclass.KEY) .
title: fontlabapp.anchors.panel.ui.AnchorPanel

text: apply_work ( work : Work , title : str , facts : AutoFacts ) -> dict [ str , Any ] Write all edits as ONE native Undo step named title . work holds no auto layer ( collect ); facts is a fresh history.scan_auto_facts . Call require_safe first. The commit uses history.commit(..., operation="geometry", read_back=...) . No rollback is tried: a failure after history started raises history.PartialWriteError with "use Edit > Undo". A value that FontLab did not keep raises history.unstored_error ("FontLab did not store ... Check those layers before you save."). Empty work returns zeros and makes no history call. Return {"anchors": native pin operations, "layers": edited layers} . One removed pin counts once, also for a repeated name.
title: fontlabapp.anchors.writer.apply_work

text: blocked_rows ( work : Work , facts : AutoFacts ) -> list [ tuple [ str , Change ]] Return one blocking row per edited glyph that the geometry policy refuses. A glyph that owns an auto layer, or is a base of one (also through other composites), is refused: FontLab rebuilds the auto composite and Undo does not restore it. facts is a fresh history.scan_auto_facts .
title: fontlabapp.anchors.writer.blocked_rows

text: collect ( glyphs : Iterable [ Any ], masters : Iterable [ str ], planner : Planner ) -> Plan Run planner on every existing layer and return the Plan . An auto layer with changes is listed as "N anchors · auto layer, skipped" and goes into skipped , never into work . A layer with a blocked row goes into problems and not into work . A missing layer is ignored.

text: require_safe ( work : Work , facts : AutoFacts ) -> None Refuse the whole batch before any history exists. Raise ValueError . A "set" edit of an existing anchor to 0, 0: FontLab cannot Redo it (FontLab issue 8527). A new anchor at 0, 0 is safe. A "set" edit of a name that several anchors of the layer carry: the move is ambiguous. "remove" and "rename" act on every pin with the name on purpose, so they pass. A glyph that owns an auto layer or is a base of one ( blocked_rows ).

For "set", check only a coordinate that the edit changed: FontLab can round an untouched coordinate (strong rounding preference), and that is not an error. For "remove", the name must be gone. For "rename", the old name must be gone and the new name present.

text: Add plain components to EXISTING glyphs, inside the caller's one history step. What: a script that adds components to glyphs that exist (Make Lower Unicase, Set Default Figures) needs a new component shape for each (base glyph, layer). No component constructor is measured on this FontLab build (fl#8505: setGlyphComponents rejects every argument form, addComponent only records a recipe entry; the source has an flShape(glyph, layer) constructor, pyflshape.cpp:66-79 , which is a native probe item and is not used). Two calls: build_components(package, target, wanted, facts) , BEFORE the caller's history.commit . It clones one plain component that the font already has (the prototype), once per NewComponent , and points each detached clone at its base glyph, layer and offset. Nothing is added to the font yet. Refusals raise ValueError and name the target glyph, so a script can show a kept row: an unknown base, a base without that layer, a bad offset, and a font without any plain component ( NO_PROTOTYPE ). add_component(layer, shape) , INSIDE mutate of the caller's history.commit(..., operation="geometry") : it adds one built shape to the target layer and checks that the layer holds one more component of that base. Declare the target layers and glyphs in the commit. The caller's commit is then the ONE Undo step of the edit. NEW glyphs get their components another way: put them in the glyph's own Add Glyph data ( glyph_creation.NewGlyph(components=(Part(...), ...)) ). That works also in a font without any component, and each new glyph is its own Undo step with its components. Why no scratch glyph: a temporary glyph made with fontpr set_glyph adds an Add Glyph Undo step, and flPackage.deleteGlyph removes it outside history, so Redo would put the temporary glyph back ( flcommands.cpp:914,919 ). That path is a native milestone candidate, not shipped behaviour. The cost: an existing glyph in a font without any plain component is refused. Prototype filter: a clone copies the builder state (attached flag, attach anchor, component variation; flcompositeshapesbuilder.cpp:79-93 ) and the shape style (excluded, content lock, non-spacing, boolean operation, opacity; flshape.cpp:1906-1934,2213 ). An attached clone gets its offset overwritten at the next layer update ( fllayer.cpp:1493-1535 ). So a prototype qualifies only when every one of these reads as the default through Python; _qualifies holds the rules: the bound flShape members ( pyflshape.cpp:438-443 ): excluded is the bool False , opacity is 1.0 ( contentLocked is not read: it is True for every component on FontLab 9.0.9808, 504 of 504 in plum, A2 report 18, so it cannot tell a user lock; the VFJ locked key below does); the fontpr get_glyph VFJ of its glyph ( mcptools_source.cpp:58-79 , a bound Python call; no flShape member reads these fields): the layer's elements match the layer shapes one to one; the element of the prototype has no locked , nonSpacing , booleanOperation , opacity or excluded key with a non-default value, and its component holds only glyphName , layerName and attached: false (no attachAnchor , no off2026Variation ; tags of bin_types.cpp:383,535-545 ; writers flshape.cpp:826-831 , flcompositeshapesbuilder.cpp:1141-1170 ). Anything that cannot be read, or reads otherwise, disqualifies the shape. No qualifying prototype gives the NO_PROTOTYPE kept row. Not measured natively: that a clone of a component is detached (own shapeData , reference count 1), that setting componentGlyph , componentLayer and transform on the detached clone re-targets it, and the Undo/Redo/save/reopen result. build_components has no auto-glyph consent: the edit runs in the caller's commit, whose history.refusal policy refuses auto layers and bases of auto composites. Offline tests prove the call order and the refusals only. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt, fontpr and scripting load when build_components runs. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.creation as component_creation import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) wanted = [component_creation.NewComponent("A", master) for master in package.masters] shapes = component_creation.build_components(package, "a", wanted, facts) target = package.findName("a") layers = [target.findLayer(m) for m in package.masters] def mutate(): for layer, shape in zip(layers, shapes, strict=True): component_creation.add_component(layer, shape) history.commit("Unicase", layers, [target], mutate, operation="geometry", facts=facts)

text: Shared plan, eject and write kernel of the component writer scripts. What: the Components writer scripts (Align By Anchor, Build From Recipes, Copy Offsets Between Masters, Decompose, Nested Finder, Replace Reference, Unlock Lock) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows. A row can hold one edit, which the script's Editor writes: EjectEditor (Decompose, Nested Finder) replaces a component with the parts of its base glyph, one level per press; MoveEditor (Align By Anchor, Copy Offsets) sets the offset of a component that plain_move accepts; other scripts subclass Editor . collect runs the planner on every editable layer and returns a Plan . Auto layers are listed and skipped, never edited. copy_problem gives the reason why the parts of a component cannot be copied safely, or "". It walks every base level as FontLab's builder does: a plain (not auto) base layer, affine transforms only, no composite shape that is not a component, no loop, not deeper than MAX_DEPTH . require_safe refuses the whole batch before any history exists: a glyph that owns an auto layer or is a base of one (also through other composites). apply_work writes all edits through ONE history.commit with operation="geometry" . EjectEditor builds the copies first, gives each removed component with its data and builder as retain= ( history.component_history ), and reads the layers back. How: eject refreshes the component cache, then copies the base parts with ejectTo() BEFORE history opens. keep_raw_state copies back what a native copy drops: the raw node connection bits (FontLab issue 8516), the element note (FontLab issue 8538) and the element name. Inside history, the write only removes the component and inserts the copies at its place. history.commit puts the retained objects first in the notification and asks for deep history, which FontLab's Undo needs for a removed component (FontLab issue 7641). Why: the logic was a private copy in each script. One App module keeps the refusals and the Undo protocol the same in every script that uses it. The generic kernel ( Change , Plan , Editor , apply_work , fmt , plural , layer_of , shown , settle ) lives in fontlabapp.masters.layers.writer ; this module re-exports it, so the Components scripts keep one import. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( history , edit_guards , layer_writer ) at load time. The fontlab module loads inside the functions, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.writer as component_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): rows = [] for shape in component_writer.components(layer): why = component_writer.copy_problem( package, (glyph.name, master), shape, master ) edit = None if why else shape.id name = component_writer.base_of(shape) rows.append(component_writer.Change(name, "", "parts", edit, why)) return rows plan = component_writer.collect(glyphs, masters, planner) facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) component_writer.require_safe(plan.work, facts) component_writer.apply_work( plan.work, "Decompose", facts, component_writer.EjectEditor(unlock=True) )
